title: 2024 financial statements approved after clean audit
subtitle: Asset management plan, community benefit agreements, committee chair changes, Ward 6 vacancy deferrals and Elliott board appointments.
overview: Council approved the City's 2024 consolidated financial statements {{vote:m6}}. The external auditor reported a clean opinion with no corrections and no significant control deficiencies. Staff described the City as financially healthy, while noting that reserves are being drawn down and debt is expected to grow as infrastructure is built.

Council also adopted a consent report that approved the community benefit agreement program review and the 2025 Corporate Asset Management Plan, and authorized the Mayor to sign a health accountability declaration. The asset plan goes to the province by July 1, 2025.

Because of the vacant Ward 6 seat, Council named Councillor Klassen chair and Councillor Chew vice-chair of the Infrastructure, Development and Environment Services committee. Appointments to The Elliott board of trustees and the Well Interference Committee were deferred to September, after a Ward 6 appointment planned for July 23.
After a closed session, Council appointed three people to The Elliott Community Board of Trustees in open session.

decisions.detail: Council approved the City's 2024 Consolidated Financial Statements and the External Audit Findings Report.
Council approved the recommendations in the Community Benefit Agreement Program Review staff report as part of the consent agenda.
Council approved the 2025 Corporate Asset Management Plan, including targeted levels of service, for submission to the Ministry of Infrastructure by July 1, 2025.
The Mayor was authorized to sign the Declaration of Compliance for the Ontario Health service accountability agreement covering April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025.
Councillor Klassen was appointed chair of the Infrastructure, Development and Environment Services committee for a term ending November 15, 2026.
Councillor Chew was appointed vice-chair of the same committee for a term ending November 15, 2026.
Decisions on The Elliott board and Well Interference Committee vacancies were deferred to September so the new Ward 6 councillor can be considered.
Ted Sehl and Kathy Wilkie were appointed for terms ending June 2028, and David Kennedy was re-appointed for a term ending June 2026.

debate: There were no questions from councillors on the audit or the financial statements. The Mayor credited staff for the result.

Staff said development charge spending in 2024 well exceeded money coming into the reserve funds, which is expected to continue as reserves are drawn down and more debt is taken on for infrastructure.
Staff said tax arrears rose in 2024, partly because of a large payment received in early 2025 and a postal strike that stopped arrears notices being mailed. They said arrears remain very low.
The auditor said the lack of corrections suggests reliable financial reporting through the year, and called staff preparation timely and of excellent quality.

On the vacancies, one councillor proposed deferring The Elliott and Well Interference appointments so a new Ward 6 councillor could take a role. Staff noted there are no August meetings, so the matter returns in September.
